chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Irene Eddy and Teddy Wilson at Mrs. Otter's house
summary: Budd and Teddy Wilson boarded at Mrs. Otter's on South Parkway, where Wilson rehearsed hours daily and showed Budd 'Liza' runs.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: However, you know, back in those days I can remember when we used to work with Irene (Eddy, Budd. and she was working -- we had -- the jobs paid like ten, $12.00 a week.
Tell us a little bit about Irene (Eddy, Budd.
Irene (Edley) was a great little piano player.
She marry anybody that you know about?
Right, that's what I'm trying to get at.

And she wrote some very good songs, and I don't know, I think maybe Irene is still living. I understand she lost her sight, or something, and she's living in Cleveland, Ohio now. But then we all were staying at a woman's house by the name of Mrs. Otter, on South Parkway there, and Mrs. Otter used to cook and feed us, and we would sit up and play cards and Teddy would be showing me changes and things on the piano. They guy rehearsed like four, five, six hours a day.
And I used to go get my horn sometime, and he'd -- I can still play some passages that he showed me, 'Liza,' you know, 'cause 'Liza' was a pretty rough tune to jam on in those days.
Yeah, that was one of our Al Jolson's --
It had a lot of changes. That's right, it had a lot of changes in it, and Teddy showed me a couple of runs in there, which is still as beautiful today.
